title: 1969 AHSME Problem 23
statement:
For any integer \(n\) greater than \(1,\) the number of prime numbers greater than \(n!+1\) and less than \(n!+n\) is:

Here \(n!=1\cdot2\cdots(n-1)n.\)

solutions.text:
Every integer in the interval has the form \(n!+k\) for some \(2\le k\le n-1.\) Because \(n!\) is divisible by \(k,\) so is \(n!+k,\) and \(n!+k\gt k.\) Thus every such integer is composite. (For \(n=2,\) the interval is empty.) Hence there are no primes in the interval.

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: Every integer strictly between the endpoints has the form \(n!+k\) with \(2\le k\le n-1\)
Use the fact that \(k\) divides both \(n!\) and \(n!+k\)
